cell_type_model: recombinant PTPRZ1/PTPzeta ectodomain and rat neuronal migration model
assay_or_perturbation: solid-phase binding and Scatchard analysis; MDK C-terminal/Arg78 mutants; neuronal migration assay
relation_type: Direct MDK binding to PTPRZ1/PTPzeta is associated with a PTPRZ1-dependent neuronal migration output
pathway_branch: MDK-PTPRZ1/PTPzeta -> neuronal migration branch
limitations: The interaction depends on PTPRZ1 glycosaminoglycan context and the study does not resolve a unique intracellular adaptor or kinase relay; PTPRZ1 is a receptor phosphatase rather than a canonical kinase receptor and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: normal murine mammary-gland epithelial-cell-derived syndecan ectodomains and purified glycosaminoglycan chains
assay_or_perturbation: BIAcore binding, glycosaminoglycan-chain comparison, chondroitinase/heparitinase treatment and core-protein controls
relation_type: Direct glycosaminoglycan- and core-protein-dependent MDK-SDC1 cell-surface proteoglycan association
pathway_branch: MDK-SDC1 proteoglycan presentation and growth-factor delivery branch
limitations: The study establishes binding and a proposed delivery function but does not isolate an SDC1 cytoplasmic relay, receptor-proximal kinase, or terminal TF; soluble and membrane proteoglycan contexts are not equivalent.

cell_type_model: murine mammary epithelial-cell syndecan ectodomains; pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and beta-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: BIAcore glycosaminoglycan binding; recombinant MDK exposure, SDC4 perturbation and Ras/insulin-secretion readouts in a pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes model
relation_type: Direct MDK-SDC4 proteoglycan binding with SDC4-dependent modulation of a Ras-linked cellular output
pathway_branch: MDK-SDC4 -> Ras-linked beta-cell function and insulin secretion branch
limitations: The older biochemical study supports stronger MDK binding to SDC4 glycosaminoglycan chains, while the newer disease-context study links SDC4 to reduced Ras signaling; a universal SDC4 cytoplasmic relay or direct MDK-to-Ras molecular edge was not established.

cell_type_model: recombinant MEPE/PHEX and mouse bone-marrow stromal or osteoblast mineralization models
assay_or_perturbation: SPR and PHEX enzyme-inhibition kinetics; phosphorylated ASARM peptide competition; FGF23 transcript and mineralization assays
relation_type: Direct MEPE/MEPE-ASARM binding inhibits PHEX enzymatic activity and produces phosphaturic and anti-mineralization outputs
pathway_branch: MEPE-ASARM-PHEX -> FGF23 and extracellular mineralization branch
limitations: The active species can be the proteolytically released ASARM fragment rather than intact MEPE; PHEX is a membrane metalloendopeptidase, not a canonical intracellular signaling receptor, and no intracellular relay or terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma cell lines and stromal fibroblast-conditioned or recombinant MFAP5 systems
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant MFAP5 and MFAP5 knockdown; co-immunoprecipitation with NOTCH1; NICD/Notch target measurements; Notch inhibition and invasion/migration assays
relation_type: MFAP5 directly associates with NOTCH1 and is upstream of a Notch1-linked tumor-cell functional program
pathway_branch: MFAP5-NOTCH1 -> NICD/Notch target program -> SLUG-associated invasion and migration
limitations: The direct interaction is supported mainly by cell-based co-IP and dose/knockdown concordance rather than purified affinity; the receptor activation mechanism is tumor-context dependent and no terminal TF occupancy was measured.

cell_type_model: 3T3-L1 adipocytes, mouse enterocyte/adipose models and Mfge8-null mice

limitations: The functional receptor is alpha-v-beta-3, so the submitted beta subunit is not an isolated receptor; direct beta3-only binding was not measured and no terminal TF endpoint was assigned.

cell_type_model: 3T3-L1 adipocytes, mouse enterocyte/adipose models and Mfge8-null mice
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant MFGE8, RGD-to-RGE control, beta5-integrin dependence, PI3K/mTORC2-AKT phosphorylation, fatty-acid uptake and genetic loss-of-function
relation_type: RGD-dependent MFGE8 engagement of an alpha-v-containing ITGB5 integrin heterodimer supports receptor-proximal AKT signaling and fatty-acid uptake
pathway_branch: MFGE8-ITGAV/ITGB5 -> PI3K-mTORC2-AKT -> CD36/FATP1 translocation and fatty-acid uptake
limitations: The functional receptor is alpha-v-beta-5, so the submitted beta subunit is not an isolated receptor; direct beta5-only binding was not measured and no terminal TF endpoint was assigned.

cell_type_model: 10T1/2 pericyte/pericyte-precursor-like cells

pathway_branch: MFGE8-alpha-v integrin-PDGFRB -> FAK/ERK/AKT -> pericyte migration
limitations: The study supports an alpha-v-integrin-mediated association with PDGFRB rather than a direct purified MFGE8-PDGFRB ligand contact; PDGFRB activation requires PDGF-BB and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: COS-7/M6 transfectants and primary murine embryonic fibroblasts or macrophages
assay_or_perturbation: MIF stimulation with CD74/CD44 expression, CD44 cytoplasmic-tail truncation, CD74/CD44 knockout cells, Src inhibition, ERK phosphorylation and apoptosis-protection assays
relation_type: MIF binds CD74 and requires full-length CD44 as the signaling component of the receptor complex
pathway_branch: MIF-CD74/CD44 -> Src-ERK1/2 -> survival and anti-apoptotic output
limitations: The receptor complex was resolved by complementary binding and reconstitution experiments rather than one purified ternary assay; heterologous and murine primary contexts were used, and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: A431, 293T, U251 and DU145 human cell systems; purified human EGFR ectodomain
assay_or_perturbation: secreted O-GlcNAcylated MIF binding and competition with EGF; EGFR, ERK1/2 and c-JUN phosphorylation; MIF manipulation and invasion/proliferation/tumor assays
relation_type: Secreted O-GlcNAcylated MIF directly binds EGFR and inhibits EGF-induced receptor activation
pathway_branch: MIF-EGFR antagonism -> EGFR-ERK-C-JUN -> invasion and proliferation
limitations: The inhibitory activity requires mammalian-secreted O-GlcNAcylated MIF and was not reproduced by bacterially expressed MIF; this is an antagonistic receptor edge, and c-JUN phosphorylation is not direct TF occupancy.

cell_type_model: recombinant MMRN2 and CD248 ectodomains; human endothelial/pericyte interface and pancreatic tumor models
assay_or_perturbation: C-type lectin-domain binding, long-loop mutation, competition and cell-surface localization assays
relation_type: Direct MMRN2-CD248 extracellular receptor-complex association
pathway_branch: MMRN2-CD248 endothelial-pericyte interface branch
limitations: CD248 binds a distinct MMRN2 region, but the study does not isolate a CD248 intracellular relay or CD248-specific angiogenic output; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: recombinant MMRN2 and CD93 ectodomains; human endothelial/pericyte interface and pancreatic tumor models
assay_or_perturbation: C-type lectin-domain binding, long-loop mutation, competition and MMRN2 peptide/cell-surface assays
relation_type: Direct MMRN2-CD93 extracellular receptor-complex association
pathway_branch: MMRN2-CD93 endothelial interface and angiogenesis-context branch
limitations: The study maps direct binding and a shared MMRN2 site with CLEC14A, but does not define a CD93-specific cytosolic relay or terminal TF; anti-angiogenic peptide effects are not a CD93-only perturbation.

cell_type_model: HUVEC and endothelial/pericyte interface models; human pancreatic cancer and mouse tumor models
assay_or_perturbation: C-type lectin-domain binding and mutation; anti-MMRN2/CLEC14A disruption, endothelial adhesion, angiogenesis and tumor-growth assays
relation_type: Direct MMRN2-CLEC14A binding is linked to an extracellular endothelial adhesion and anti-angiogenic functional output
pathway_branch: MMRN2-CLEC14A -> endothelial adhesion/angiogenesis branch
limitations: The functional perturbations disrupt an extracellular interaction and do not resolve a CLEC14A-specific intracellular kinase or adaptor relay; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: Ron/MST1R-transfected MDCK cells and primary mouse peritoneal macrophages
assay_or_perturbation: radiolabeled MSP binding/crosslinking, receptor immunoprecipitation and phosphorylation; recombinant MSP, Gab1/Gab2 phosphorylation, docking-site mutants, LPS/IFN-gamma stimulation and NF-kB/STAT1 readouts
relation_type: MST1/MSP activates the MST1R/RON receptor tyrosine kinase and engages receptor-docking and inflammatory signaling branches
pathway_branch: MST1-MST1R/RON -> receptor autophosphorylation-Gab1/2-ERK/PI3K/FAK -> NF-kB and STAT1 inflammatory regulation
limitations: Active MSP is the processed alpha-beta heterodimer; the macrophage TF effects are context-dependent modulation of LPS/IFN-gamma responses rather than a universal direct MST1R-to-TF route. RELA/STAT1 are measured downstream endpoints, not direct receptor contacts.

cell_type_model: mouse platelet-associated Myl9 nets, activated CD69-positive T cells and human inflammatory airway lesions
assay_or_perturbation: CD69 extracellular-domain pull-down/mass spectrometry, Myl9 mutant binding, blocking antibodies and ovalbumin/house-dust-mite airway inflammation models
relation_type: Direct MYL9-CD69 binding supports recruitment and retention of activated CD69-positive lymphocytes in inflamed tissue
pathway_branch: MYL9-CD69 inflammatory adhesion/recruitment platform -> airway inflammation
limitations: CD69 is a lectin-like activation marker with no defined MYL9-specific intracellular relay in these experiments; the phenotype is recruitment/retention and no terminal TF was measured.

pathway_branch: GDNF-GFRA1-NCAM1 -> NCAM-associated Fyn/FAK/neurite migration and adhesion branch
limitations: GFRA1 is a GDNF coreceptor and NCAM1 is an alternative signaling receptor in this complex; the submitted orientation is receptor-receptor association rather than NCAM1 acting as an independently secreted ligand, and no terminal TF was measured.

relation_type: Direct heterophilic NCAM1-ROBO3 receptor/adhesion-protein association
pathway_branch: NCAM1-ROBO3 axon-guidance adhesion-complex branch
limitations: The study establishes heterophilic binding but does not define an NCAM1-ROBO3-specific receptor-proximal relay or downstream TF; Robo3 isoform and developmental context matter.

assay_or_perturbation: ligand-overlay and Scatchard binding, heparitinase/chondroitinase controls, cell adhesion and neurite-outgrowth assays
relation_type: Heparan-sulfate-dependent NCAN-SDC3 binding supports a neurite-outgrowth cellular output
pathway_branch: NCAN-SDC3 HSPG interaction -> cerebellar neurite outgrowth branch

assay_or_perturbation: AP-Norrin cell binding, receptor swaps and knockdown, TOPFLASH Wnt reporter assays, dose response and LRP5/6/FZD comparator tests
